documents.abstract: Smart homes are evolving from passive response to proactive service, where understanding the semantic information in user trajectories is essential. However, existing tracking systems output only sparse location sequences, insufficient for higher-level semantic reasoning. The core bottleneck lies in the lack of large-scale annotated datasets, while traditional data collection is costly and raises privacy concerns. We present TSGen, which formalizes indoor trajectory-semantic data synthesis as a structured decomposition problem. We first demonstrate that naive end-to-end LLM approaches are fundamentally limited for this task, then propose a hybrid workflow combining LLM-driven behavior simulation, physics-constrained trajectory synthesis, and a self-refining prompt architecture that evolves from runtime errors, to construct the T-S dataset (14,000 hours of trajectory-semantic pairs). We also implement a hierarchical processing pipeline as an initial baseline for semantic understanding, establishing reference benchmarks for future research. Evaluations cover data quality (user studies, diversity analysis, ablation studies) and baseline performance. On QA tasks over synthetic data and real-world deployments, our baseline significantly outperforms direct LLM methods while reducing computational costs. The open-sourced dataset and codebase provide foundational resources for this emerging research area 1 .

Recommendation throughout the cold-start period remains a challenge in recommender systems. Strictly cold entities (users/items) have no interactions, while warm-up entities only have a few unreliable interactions. Strict cold-start methods typically overlook warm-up entities, while warm-up methods are generally not designed for entities with no observed interactions. In this paper, we propose ProbLLM , an LLM-driven framework that reformulates cold-start recommendation as interaction simulation through a shared retrieve–score–select interface. LLM-based content retrieval first constructs a bounded candidate pool, after which a probability-form prompt elicits a bounded confidence score for every retained pair. Selected interactions retain these confidence scores as soft weights for downstream representation learning. Within this architecture, Filtering Simulation is followed by Refining Simulation for every cold target. Pairwise refinement elicits an LLM confidence score for each filtered candidate before pseudo-interaction selection. A two-phase sequential procedure first initializes the collaborative embeddings on observed interactions and then refines them with confidence-weighted ranking and cold-aware graph aggregation. Across the evaluated settings and matched recommendation backbones, ProbLLM achieves higher performance than the corresponding baselines.

Abstract An engaging and cost-effective digital tool for developing subject-matter knowledge (SMK) could mitigate educational inequities in resource-constrained contexts. This case study explores the effectiveness of free generative artificial intelligence (GAI) platforms, prompted to function as a Flipped-Interaction Intelligent Tutoring System (FIITS), to promote science student-teacher SMK learning. Data were collected across a 10-week intervention from 42 third- and fourth-year natural and physical sciences student teachers at two campuses of a South African university. The students engaged with the FIITS in odd-numbered weeks by pasting a provided prompt into a free GAI platform, and with benchmarking interactive electronic worksheets in even-numbered weeks. Affective, behavioural, and cognitive engagement and perceptions of SMK learning were analysed using post-session questionnaires, end-of-module reflections, and group interviews. Both modalities elicited consistently high and comparable engagement levels, but students reported stronger perceptions of SMK development with the FIITS. They valued its personalisation, relevance, and human-like interactivity, although workload pressures and occasional GAI errors somewhat hindered the FIITS’s effectiveness. These findings suggest that free GAI platforms, prompted to behave as FIITS, may provide equitable, scalable, and pedagogically effective tools for improving SMK in student-teacher education. Recommendations include scaffolding an initial adjustment phase, incorporating varied levels of challenge, and managing novelty and workload to sustain engagement. This study offers early evidence of the pedagogical potential of free flipped-interaction GAI in science teacher education, particularly in contexts where access to costly educational technologies is limited.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Generative AI tools promise to expand student agency in management education, yet the same tool can help and hurt learning inside a single classroom. We argue this contradiction is the signature of two psychological pathways running in parallel. Drawing on the cognitive-affective-conative framework, we develop a dual-pathway serial mediation model in which a cognitive pathway runs from psychological reactance through autonomy perceptions to effectiveness judgments, while an affective pathway runs from ethical perceptions through emotional engagement to effectiveness judgments. Ninety-seven undergraduate management students participated in two AI-enhanced activities with different chatbot tools across one semester. Both pathways operated as predicted. More surprising was how the cognitive pathway changed across exposures. At first use, reactance traveled through autonomy, consistent with self-determination theory. By the second activity, reactance bypassed autonomy and suppressed effectiveness directly. The affective pathway remained stable across exposures. For management educators, ethical framing before a student's first AI encounter may do more work than redesigning the tools themselves to preserve student choice. As a single-cohort study using two researcher-built chatbots, the results are preliminary and point to hypotheses for multi-site replication rather than population estimates.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Mobile task automation aims to streamline multi-step, cross-app interactions on smartphones and in-vehicle systems. Recent LLM-based GUI agents have advanced rapidly, yet reliability remains limited because modern mobile workflows are increasingly service-composed (app switching, forms, pop-ups/permissions, copy-paste), requiring fine-grained operations on dense, dynamic, and heterogeneous UIs, often in distraction-sensitive contexts (e.g., hands-busy or attention-limited use). Through an in-the-wild failure analysis of deployable GUI agents, we identify two dominant bottlenecks: agents often miss or misread actionable UI elements, and they execute actions without verifying target correctness or outcomes. We present UIAnchor, a modular multi-agent system that improves mobile GUI automation by anchoring both perception and execution. UIAnchor combines a two-stage UI parser for high-recall element capture and context-aware semantics with a meta-controller that performs pre-action verification, post-action outcome perception, per-step state tracking, and targeted recovery. We further introduce an L1-L5 task taxonomy based on step length, cross-app scope, and UI granularity, showing that L5 remains beyond today's practical frontier. On the hardest practical tier, L4 tasks (20-30 steps, multi-app, targets < 100 × 100 px, ~5 mm on typical phones), UIAnchor improves success by 31.5% over GPT-4o and 16.6% over Mobile-Agent-v3. With edge/cloud assistance, UIAnchor runs at ~2 s per step, comparable to human operation, while reducing per-step latency by up to 75.5% and energy by 52.4%. It also generalizes to unseen apps and cross-platform GUIs.
topics: Personal Information Management and User Behavior

Amidst the context of digital transformation and the rapid advancement of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), integrating AI tools into foreign language instruction opens up new opportunities for pedagogical innovation. Regarding the teaching of Vietnamese as a foreign language, vocabulary serves as the foundation of communicative competence; however, research on the application of GenAI in this specific field remains relatively limited. This paper analyzes the potential of GenAI applications in teaching Vietnamese vocabulary to foreigners by combining a literature review with an analysis of typical teaching scenarios. The findings indicate that GenAI can effectively support activities such as introducing new words, explaining meanings, expanding vocabulary networks, creating usage contexts, designing exercises, personalizing learning activities, and providing immediate feedback to learners. Based on these findings, the paper proposes a process for integrating GenAI into Vietnamese vocabulary instruction using a learner-centered approach. It also outlines pedagogical requirements and usage principles to ensure linguistic accuracy, cultural appropriateness, and the continued vital role of the teacher in the instructional process. The study contributes both theoretical and practical insights into the application of GenAI in teaching Vietnamese as a foreign language, thereby meeting the demands for educational innovation in the era of digital transformation.

Objective: There is a need to examine studies on the use of artificial intelligence in nursing care and to identify the characteristics of research in this field. This study was designed to identify and analyze the existing literature on the use of artificial intelligence in nursing care and to examine the key characteristics of these studies.Material and Methods: The data were obtained from the Web of Science database on January, 2025, using the keywords “artificial intelligence” and “nursing care.” A total of 33 publications were included in the study. The studies were thematically classified as part of the content analysis, and main themes and sub-themes were determined.Results: The content analysis identified four main themes: decision support and clinical practice, ethical and safety issues, workflow, and time management. Sub-themes included care plans, patient monitoring, decision-making processes, data privacy and confidentiality, preserving human-centered care, reliability and accuracy issues, automation of routine tasks, and efficiency and process optimization.Conclusion: Artificial intelligence is a significant and transformative tool in nursing care. The safe and effective integration of this technology depends on establishing ethical frameworks, sustaining a human-centered approach, and preventing technological dependency.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming an important technology in the field of Geography. It helps geographers collect, process, analyze, and interpret large amounts of geographical data quickly and accurately. AI is widely used with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Remote Sensing, satellite images, GPS, and spatial databases. It can help in land-use and land-cover mapping, urban planning, population analysis, disaster management, climate studies, agriculture, and environmental monitoring. AI-based techniques such as machine learning and deep learning can identify patterns and changes in geographical areas that may be difficult to detect through traditional methods. AI also helps in predicting natural hazards such as floods, droughts, landslides, and forest fires. In urban areas, it supports transportation planning, infrastructure development, and smart-city management. In agriculture, AI can assist in crop monitoring, soil analysis, and yield prediction. However, the effective use of AI requires reliable data, skilled users, proper technology, and attention to data privacy and accuracy. Thus, Artificial Intelligence has great potential to improve geographical research, spatial analysis, planning, and sustainable development.

documents.abstract: Value steering should change an LLM's normative priorities while preserving the scenario, facts, and task constraints underlying its answer. Conventional activation edits often change both. We introduce an editable semantic-value interface on frozen residual states, with a one-way semantic-to-value pathway that grounds value recognition in context. Stop-gradient blocks feedback through this pathway; swap consistency, topic de-confounding, and decorrelation encourage selective codes. At inference, editing the value code produces a residual delta while holding the semantic code fixed. On two instruction-tuned backbones, this interface improves semantic preservation and reduces benign refusals at comparable value alignment. A matched mixing-by-gating ablation separates representation learning from selective edit activation, and dimension-matched probes establish improved code selectivity. Against validation-selected prompting on LLaMA-3.1-8B, the method achieves comparable alignment (0.750 vs. 0.748), higher BERTScore (0.938 vs. 0.923), and fewer contradictions (5.1% vs. 7.6%). Human ratings and cross-taxonomy controls provide complementary evidence for low-damage value steering.

Contemporary society faces the ubiquitous proliferation of algorithmic systems that structure social life, from intimate subjective modulation to planetary crisis management. This conceptual paper therefore proposes the analytical category of vigitalization. Rooted in relational sociology, vigitalization is defined as a co-constitutive sociotechnical configuration that fuses datafication with structural surveillance to interpret the autonomization of algorithmic governance. Employing a multilevel theoretical framework bridging the macro (systematicity), meso (grouping), and micro (interaction) dimensions, the study dissects the relational interdependencies between technological infrastructures, political economy, and algocratic bureaucracies. Vigitalization operates under a strict recursive logic: digitizing to monitor and monitoring to digitize, naturalizing behavioral extraction across all institutional boundaries. Crucially, this framework positions vigitalization as the primary sociotechnical matrix governing the ASAM Nexus (Agency-Structure-Algorithm-Matter). By doing so, it equips sociology with the critical apparatus required to address the existential macro-risks, biopolitical subsumption, and biometric enclosures intrinsic to the Digital Anthropocene.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This study aims to examine how generative artificial intelligence systems shape gender representations and which experiences they render discursively visible or invisible. In this context, the responses generated by ChatGPT, a U.S.-based large language model, and DeepSeek, a China-based model, regarding motherhood, femininity, and caregiving experiences in the contexts of Gaza and East Turkestan were comparatively analysed. The study was conducted using a qualitative content analysis and comparative discourse analysis approach. Data obtained from a total of 60 prompts were evaluated in terms of mechanisms of discursive visibility, omission, and reframing. The findings reveal that both models produce representations that humanise motherhood; however, these representations vary significantly depending on the context. ChatGPT, particularly in the context of Gaza, tends to make human suffering visible while avoiding explicit identification of the perpetrators of violence and political responsibility, thereby producing a neutralising discourse. In contrast, DeepSeek, in the context of East Turkestan, tends to avoid representation, suppress certain narratives, and at times generate a discourse that may be interpreted as implicitly legitimising.These findings suggest that artificial intelligence systems are not merely tools for information generation but also epistemic actors that selectively construct gender representations. The study contributes to the literature on AI ethics and feminist technology studies by demonstrating that bias in artificial intelligence should be evaluated not only through explicit prejudice but also through processes of discursive invisibility and omission.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: With the continuous advancement of digital transformation, digital technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence have greatly reshaped corporate office practices. While these technologies significantly improve organizational work efficiency, they also produce digital hindrance stressors, which bring negative effects on employees’ mental states and work behaviors. In digital office settings, employees are faced with growing digital‑related work pressure, and cyberloafing as a type of work‑deviant behavior occurs more frequently. Drawing on self‑regulation theory, this study selects self‑regulation impairment as the mediating variable and self‑regulation trait as the moderating variable. It systematically analyzes the underlying influence path through which digital hindrance stressors act on employees’ cyberloafing behavior via self‑regulation impairment, under the moderating effect of self‑regulation trait.

Contextual information in recommender systems is shifting from static, predefined variables toward latent representations inferred from behavior. Large language models support this shift by rendering an unstructured interaction history as a natural-language summary, which yields a thematic user context that can be encoded and used in place of an aggregate profile. The conditions under which such generated profiles outperform aggregate embeddings have received limited characterization mainly at the domain level. We evaluate semantic user-profiling strategies on a production streaming platform, ranking against the full catalog. The evaluation covers a 2*2 design space crossing representation type (aggregate or LLM-generated) with contextual scope (holistic history or attention-fused short-term and long-term contexts). The relative ordering of the two representation types is conditional on the user's consumption regime. Aggregate profiles are consistently stronger under habitual consumption, which characterizes approximately four-fifths of the population, while LLM-generated profiles are stronger for exploratory users whose subsequent interactions diverge semantically from their history. We also observe a popularity-attractor effect in LLM-generated profiles, which modestly raises within-list diversity while substantially lowering catalog coverage and reducing novelty. These results indicate that a context-aware system can select a profiling strategy from the inferred consumption regime rather than applying one representation to all users.
topics: Personal Information Management and User Behavior

documents.abstract: Ownership establishes rights over the use, control, and transfer of objects. Understanding these relations is essential for AI systems to interact appropriately with people and their resources. Yet how large language models (LLMs) attribute ownership under competing claims remains unclear. We introduce the Competing Ownership Attribution Task (COAT), comprising 42 scenarios, and compare ownership allocations from 24 LLM configurations with those of 108 human participants. Overall, human-model similarity is close to human-human similarity, but models show greater homogeneity in their ownership judgments. Within individual answers, models also divide ownership more evenly among claimants than humans do. Pooling responses across model configurations reveals more scenarios with a shared judgment and fewer with distinct viewpoint groups than in humans. When humans form distinct groups, models may converge on one viewpoint or between competing viewpoints. Further comparisons reveal different contextual sensitivities. As material value increases across scenarios, allocations to creators decline less sharply in models than in humans. Across scenarios differing in public recognition of later holders as owners, allocations to these holders increase in models but decrease slightly in humans. Together, these findings suggest that the evaluated LLM responses do not fully capture the diversity of participants' ownership judgments or how those judgments vary across situations. Developing socially capable AI therefore requires moving beyond overall similarity to capture the diversity and context dependence of human judgments.

documents.abstract: Organizations increasingly route employee feedback to leaders through large language model (LLM) summaries, an unaudited layer that silences already-spoken voice. We introduce a Voice Retention / Representation Ratio metric for representational bias in summarization and apply it to a bilingual (English/German) corpus of 2,586 free-text responses from a global professional service company. First, employees supply criticism more reliably than praise (withholding praise is 82 times more common). Second, across 45 leader-summaries the pipeline filters by popularity, not sentiment: criticism survives, yet a concern voiced once is dropped 86% of the time, with short and German-only content lost on the same axis (theme retention 0.14 vs 0.74; German directional). Controlling for frequency, sentiment has no independent effect; the harm is prevalence-driven, which sentiment-only audits miss. A targeted prompt recovers only named themes. We contribute the metric, field evidence, and a disaggregated voice-retention card.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are now widely applied across different domains. As AI systems increasingly shape professional and academic domains, there is a growing need to pre-pare future professionals to work with these technologies responsibly and effectively. Accordingly, an increasing number of studies advocate AI education for undergraduates across disciplines. However, there is limited qualitative research on these students’ motivations for learning about AI and on what they are interested in learning, despite the importance of such understanding for designing motivating, engaging, and effective learning experiences. Therefore, the objective of this research is to answer the following two research questions: (1) What motivates undergraduates across disciplines to learn about AI? (2) What are undergraduates across disciplines interested in learning about AI? To answer the research questions, we conducted a survey with 128 students who voluntarily enrolled in an elective introductory AI course over three semesters. The findings indicate that these students are motivated to learn about AI not only for career-related utility but also due to its perceived societal relevance and ethical implications. Regarding learning interests, students most frequently expressed interest in learning how AI systems work, how these systems impact society positively and negatively, and how to use them effectively and responsibly. In the discussion section, we provide guidance on how these results can inform the design or adaptation of AI curricula, course invitations, and learning experiences to foster sustained engagement and meaningful learning among these students.

documents.abstract: ersonal protective equipment (PPE) is a fundamental component of occupational health and safety; however, its effectiveness is strongly influenced by worker behaviour, organisational context, and human factors. Despite the long-standing use of PPE, research in this field remains fragmented and rapidly expanding, making it difficult to develop a comprehensive understanding of how worker behaviour influences PPE effectiveness over time. This bibliometric review addresses this gap by systematically analysing scientific publications from 1970 to 2026 to identify publication trends, influential studies, leading contributing countries, dominant research themes, and patterns of international collaboration. Data were retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science, resulting in a final dataset of 1,236 peer-reviewed journal articles. Scopus Analyzer, OpenRefine, and VOSviewer were employed for descriptive, bibliometric, and network analyses. The findings reveal a prolonged formative phase followed by substantial publication growth after 2019, largely driven by increasing global attention to occupational safety and the COVID-19 pandemic. Research output remains concentrated in several high-income countries, while contributions from developing regions remain limited. Keyword analysis demonstrates a shift from technical PPE performance to behavioural dimensions, including compliance, risk perception, safety culture, usability, and organisational influence. International collaboration networks reveal major research hubs and global disparities in research integration. Overall, this study highlights the increasing importance of behavioural and socio-technical perspectives in PPE research and provides a foundation for future interdisciplinary studies, evidence-based safety policies, workplace intervention strategies, and sustainable occupational health practices aimed at improving long-term worker safety outcomes.

Abstract: Platform-based food delivery has become a symbol of precarious labour, marked by spatial fragmentation, pervasive algorithmic control and the erosion of social protection. This article examines how algorithmic management and subcontracting reconfigure labour control and solidarity in this sector. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork with delivery riders in Austria and Germany, it combines semi-structured interviews, participant observation and digital ethnography. The article develops the notion of fragmented and situational solidarity to capture how spontaneous encounters and digital communities emerge within a highly individualized labour process. It also shows how subcontracting and legal misclassification in Germany and Austria reconfigure workers’ fragmentation, especially regarding citizenship and residence permit. The study reveals how riders – despite structural barriers – establish new spaces for collective action, both online and offline. By bringing together labour process theory and ethnographic research, the article contributes to understanding how algorithmic management restructures not only labour control, but also the conditions for solidarity. Keywords: Platform work, gig economy, algorithmic management, labour struggle, solidarity. ____________________________ Trabalhar para o Algoritmo: Condições de Trabalho e Ação Coletiva de Estafetas na Economia de Plataforma Resumo: A entrega de comida baseada em plataformas tornou-se um símbolo do trabalho precário, marcada pela fragmentação espacial, pelo controlo algorítmico omnipresente e pela erosão da proteção social. Este artigo examina como a gestão algorítmica e a subcontratação reconfiguram o controlo laboral e a solidariedade neste setor. Com base em trabalho de campo etnográfico com estafetas na Áustria e na Alemanha, o estudo combina entrevistas semiestruturadas, observação participante e etnografia digital. O artigo desenvolve a noção de solidariedade fragmentada e situacional para captar como encontros espontâneos e comunidades digitais emergem dentro de um processo de trabalho altamente individualizado. Demonstra também como a subcontratação e a classificação jurídica indevida na Alemanha e na Áustria reconfiguram a fragmentação dos trabalhadores, especialmente no que diz respeito à cidadania e aos títulos de residência. O estudo revela como os trabalhadores – apesar das barreiras estruturais – estabelecem novos espaços para a ação coletiva, tanto online quanto offline. Ao articular a teoria do processo de trabalho com a investigação etnográfica, o artigo contribui para a compreensão de como a gestão algorítmica reconfigura não apenas o controlo do trabalho, mas também as condições para a solidariedade. Palavras-chave: Trabalho em plataformas, economia de plataforma, gestão algorítmica, luta laboral, solidariedade.

Purpose This study explores the application of the Lean Management Plus – 5S (LMP-5S) approach in a Moroccan SME. It evaluates its impact on workplace improvement by balancing operational efficiency with employee well-being, and positions LMP-5S as a benchmarking methodology that connects operational and social performance. Design/methodology/approach Over nine months, a participatory action research design combined employee involvement, Gemba observations, semi-structured interviews and performance analysis. Workplace outcomes were assessed through the Overall Equipment Effectiveness Plus (OEEP) indicator and the QCDESE framework (Quality, Cost, Delivery, Ergonomics, Safety, Environment), enabling internal before/after benchmarking against firm targets and external benchmarking against industry-specific and international benchmarks. Findings LMP-5S yielded a 31% increase in production capacity, an 80% reduction in search time and a 90% decrease in workplace risks, while OEEP improved from 17% to 85.3%. These results align with global Lean benchmarks, demonstrating that LMP-5S enables SMEs to achieve internationally comparable performance. Research limitations/implications Evidence comes from a single Moroccan manufacturing SME, which may constrain the generalisability of results. Long-term LMP-5S effects were not examined, constraining external validity. Practical implications The integrated QCDESE + OEEP dashboard provides SME managers with a shop-floor-ready measurement and audit routine to steer continuous improvement across operational and socio-ergonomic dimensions. Originality/value The paper formalises QCDESE and OEEP as an integrated performance measurement framework, extending widely used models such as the Balanced Scorecard and SCOR by embedding ergonomic, safety, and environ-mental dimensions. It positions LMP-5S as a replicable and sustainable performance model for SMEs, offering a transferable pathway toward continuous improvement and operational excellence.

Purpose This paper aims to examine how constructive alignment, context support, psychological safety and defensive routines are associated with observable indicators of workplace learning in civil-military crisis exercises and why exercise participation should not be equated with demonstrated learning. Design/methodology/approach This study is a comparative qualitative reanalysis of two previously studied Swedish exercise settings conducted between 2022 and 2024. No new empirical data was collected for this study. The structurally nonequivalent cases are compared using the same deductive workplace-learning framework; the comparison is used to elaborate theory rather than to estimate causal effects. Findings Case A exhibited more observable indicators of learning progression, along with clearer objectives, sequenced activities, feedback opportunities and stronger contextual support. Case B displayed fewer such indicators alongside vague objectives, limited assessment, heterogeneous participant experience and recurring defensive routines. Because the cases also differ in duration, immersion, group stability, participant composition and unit of analysis, these patterns are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects of exercise design. Research limitations/implications The comparison concerns one five-day exercise and a composite of seven exercises, uses unequal qualitative corpora and lacks independent pre- and postmeasures or behavioral evidence of transfer. This study therefore identifies theoretically relevant patterns and observable learning-process indicators, not verified individual learning outcomes or causal effects. Practical implications Exercise planners should connect specific learning objectives to role-relevant activities and structured feedback, while deliberately providing legal expertise, role clarity, facilitation and conditions for speaking up. Evaluation should distinguish immediate exercise outputs from subsequent transfer to ordinary work. Originality/value This study does not add new empirical data. Its contribution is a standardized cross-case reanalysis that integrates constructive alignment with workplace-learning affordances, psychological safety, defensive routines and training-transfer research and specifies the boundary conditions under which exercise outputs can be interpreted as indicators of learning progression.
topics: Human Resource Development and Performance Evaluation

documents.abstract: ABSTRAKHasil identifikasi yang dilaksanakan di PKBM Budaya Jakarta Pusat menunjukkan bahwa sebagian peserta memiliki keterbatasan literasi digital dan belum optimal memanfaatkan smartphone, media sosial, marketplace, serta Artificial Intelligence (AI) untuk kegiatan kewirausahaan. Tujuan dilaksanakan Workshop Strategi Pemasaran Digital ini untuk meningkatkan pengetahuan, keterampilan, kreativitas, dan kemandirian peserta dalam merancang serta menerapkan pemasaran berbasis teknologi digital. Kegiatan dilaksanakan menggunakan pendekatan pemberdayaan masyarakat secara partisipatif melalui sosialisasi, penyampaian materi interaktif, diskusi, demonstrasi, praktik langsung, penerapan teknologi, pendampingan, monitoring, dan evaluasi. Materi workshop mencakup konsep digital marketing dan e-commerce, strategi Segmentasi, Targeting, Positioning (STP) dan Unique Selling Proposition (USP), branding, fotografi produk menggunakan telepon pintar, pembuatan desain dan video promosi berbasis AI, copywriting, publikasi melalui Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, dan WhatsApp Business, serta pengelolaan toko pada Shopee. Hasil yang dicapai setelah pelaksanaan worksop menunjukkan sebanyak 15 dari 18 peserta mampu menghasilkan konten promosi yang lebih menarik, menyusun caption sesuai target pasar, mempublikasikan konten pada media sosial, dan mulai menerapkan e-commerce. Peserta juga menunjukkan peningkatan kepercayaan diri, motivasi, kemampuan evaluasi diri, dan kesadaran terhadap pentingnya teknologi dalam pengembangan usaha. Workshop diharapkan menjadi dasar penguatan komunitas kewirausahaan melalui pendampingan berkelanjutan. Dengan demikian, program ini berkontribusi pada peningkatan daya saing dan produktivitas masyarakat.Kata kunci: Workshop; Strategi pemasaran digital; E-commerce; PKBM. ABSTRACTAn initial assessment conducted at PKBM Budaya in Central Jakarta revealed that some participants had limited digital literacy and were not fully utilizing smartphones, social media, online marketplaces, or Artificial Intelligence (AI) for entrepreneurial activities. This Digital Marketing Strategy Workshop aimed to enhance participants' knowledge, skills, creativity, and independence in designing and implementing technology-based marketing. The activity employed a participatory community empowerment approach, incorporating outreach, interactive presentations, discussions, demonstrations, hands-on practice, technology application, mentoring, monitoring, and evaluation. Workshop topics covered digital marketing and e-commerce concepts; Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) strategies and Unique Selling Propositions (USP); branding; smartphone product photography; AI-based promotional design and video creation; copywriting; publishing content on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and WhatsApp Business; and managing a Shopee store. Post-workshop results showed that 15 out of 18 participants were able to create more engaging promotional content, draft captions tailored to their target markets, publish content on social media, and begin implementing e-commerce practices. Participants also demonstrated increased self-confidence, motivation, self-evaluation capabilities, and awareness of the importance of technology in business development. The workshop is expected to serve as a foundation for strengthening the entrepreneurial community through ongoing mentoring. Thus, this program contributes to enhancing community competitiveness and productivity.Keywords: Workshop; Digital marketing strategy; E-commerce; PKBM.

documents.abstract: As interactive 3D worlds are increasingly used to study intelligent behavior, it becomes important to develop efficient pipelines for identifying anomalies in these simulated environments, such as floating objects, traversable walls, or objects inconsistent with the surrounding scene. Multimodal AI systems, including vision-language models (VLMs) and vision-language-action models (VLAs), have shown potential for automating this task. However, 3D world auditing is complex, requiring the close coupling of two distinct capabilities: action, to navigate the 3D world and search for anomalies systematically and efficiently; and visual reasoning, to understand the environment and identify anomalies from multimodal observations. It remains largely unexplored whether multimodal agents can effectively couple these two capabilities, using visual reasoning to identify potential anomalies while taking actions to validate them. In this paper, we introduce WorldAuditBench, a benchmark for 3D world auditing comprising 213 anomaly tasks across 13 environments built with Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js, spanning five anomaly families. We evaluate five frontier models under a fixed exploration budget using two auditing paradigms: VLA-based exploration followed by VLM-based anomaly identification, and an end-to-end VLM agent in which visual reasoning directly guides action selection. Across the evaluated models and two paradigms, success rates range from 6.6% to 42.3%, substantially below human performance (83.4%). Through the task of world auditing, WorldAuditBench provides a testbed for studying how multimodal agents couple action and visual reasoning in interactive 3D environments, while highlighting current limitations in their ability to gather and interpret evidence during exploration.

Generative AI (GenAI) has revolutionized academic writing, shifting the nature of human-AI interactions in text production. While previous studies focus on academic honesty and general writing outcomes, little research addresses how multilingual university students negotiate authorial identities during AI integration. This qualitative study explores the negotiation of authorial identity among 15 postgraduate students at Mahendra Multiple Campus, Tribhuvan University, Nepal, using semi-structured interviews and reflexive thematic analysis. Guided by Ivanič’s Writer Identity Theory, Vygotsky’s Sociocultural Theory, Norton’s Identity and Investment Theory, and Bourdieu’s Linguistic Capital Theory, the study investigates students' perceptions of authorship, creativity, and linguistic voice. Empirically, the findings reveal five key outcomes: (1) students utilize GenAI primarily as a linguistic scaffolding tool to bridge conceptual ideas and formal academic English; (2) authorship is experienced as a negotiated sociotechnical space where intellectual ownership of ideas remains human while linguistic expression is co-constructed; (3) GenAI acts as a cognitive and creative partner that stimulates alternative argumentation rather than replacing human ingenuity; (4) participants experience an internal tension between achieving polished Western-centric academic English and preserving their authentic multilingual voices; and (5) sustainable writing relies on robust human agency, critical evaluation, and editorial oversight. These findings demonstrate that AI is not a mere substitution tool but an intervening mediator that reshapes scholarly writing. The study offers critical insights from a South Asian multilingual higher education context, advocating for AI-literate classrooms that foster intellectual ownership while enabling responsible technological utilization.

Coupling Large Language Models (LLMs) to low-code platforms compresses business-automation delivery cycles. Yet, the resulting composable architectures expose attack surfaces that perimeter-based controls were never designed to police. We propose the Zero-Trust Automation Lifecycle (ZTAL), a methodology that threads continuous Zero-Trust verification throughout the twelve-stage low-code development process. Three phases (Prepare, Mitigate, Optimize) operationalize the "never trust, always verify" doctrine while emitting security artifacts (visual policy matrices, verified configuration screenshots) as by-products of ordinary development work. We present a functional reference implementation of ZTAL together with an evaluation design spanning security, performance, and usability. Against representative threat scenarios (prompt injection, data exfiltration, over-privileged access, and classification breach), the reference implementation enforces deny-by-default policy at every internal surface: each scenario is blocked at its enforcement point while benign traffic passes. Illustrative target figures used to scope the study (a substantial reduction in Policy Violation Rate against a legacy perimeter baseline, policy-evaluation overhead in the tens of milliseconds per request, and micro-segmentation coverage rising from partial to near-complete) are reported as expected outcomes of the instrumented evaluation set out in the methodology, not as completed measurements. The framework offers practitioners an artifact-driven blueprint for securing composable AI systems and a working reference implementation on which the full empirical validation can be conducted.

The article examines the issues related to the implementation of innovative technical control means during the escorting of persons held in custody and those sentenced to imprisonment by units of the National Guard of Ukraine. The current regulatory and legal framework, as well as the present state of technical support for escort activities, are analyzed. The shortcomings of traditional control methods are identified, in particular the dependence on the human factor and the limited capacity for оперативний monitoring. The feasibility of using electronic monitoring, GPS tracking, video recording, and biometric identification is substantiated. It is concluded that there is a need to modernize the escorting system taking into account security challenges and human rights standards.
topics: Education and Social Development in Ukraine

documents.abstract: Стаття аналізує взаємодію людини та систем штучного інтелекту (ШІ, AI) у тестуванні програмного забезпечення в Agile-командах. Досліджено вплив AI-асистованого прийняття рішень на ефективність виявлення дефектів, швидкість тестування та якість командної роботи. Проведено огляд сучасних наукових джерел щодо використання ШІ в тестуванні, автоматизації контролю якості та впливу AI-інструментів на діяльність тестувальників у багатофункціональних командах. Визначено переваги й ризики застосування AI-асистованих систем: автоматизаційне упередження, надмірна довіра до AI-рекомендацій, зниження критичного мислення тестувальників, можливість хибнопозитивних результатів. Досліджено особливості Human-AI Collaboration у тестуванні, визначено ключові фактори результативності AI-асистованого тестування в Agile-середовищах. Проведено емпіричне дослідження із залученням тестувальників, які використовували AI-інструменти для генерації тестових сценаріїв, аналізу дефектів і підтримки прийняття рішень. Встановлено, що AI-асистовані підходи підвищують швидкість виявлення дефектів і оптимізують тестування, але потребують постійного людського контролю та перевірки рекомендацій. Запропоновано рекомендації щодо ефективної інтеграції AI-інструментів у тестування в Agile-командах. Результати мають практичне значення для організації процесів забезпечення якості програмного забезпечення та розробки нових підходів до управління Human-AI взаємодією у сфері тестування.

The article examines the significance of contemporary realities and challenges that impose new demands on the personality of higher education faculty members. It is noted that a university lecturer acts as an intermediary between socio-economic needs and state requirements—focused on training future professionals for Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction—and the shaping of the self-awareness and national culture of modern society. The article emphasizes that the lecturer's capacity for self-organization is a key factor in overcoming the challenges of the current academic landscape, a quality that takes on particular importance in developing a culture of academic governance. An analytical synthesis of approaches to understanding the self-organization of higher education faculty within the context of corporate culture has been conducted; empirical data regarding the key characteristics of faculty professional self-organization, considering the specific features of corporate culture, have been analyzed. The professional self-organization of a higher education faculty member is conceptualized as a process of cultivating internal motivation, discipline, and the refinement of professional personal attributes—a process accompanied by self-awareness, focus, goal-orientation, and professional competence; the mobilization of all intellectual resources and their practical application within the educational environment; the establishment of fundamental principles of ethics and integrity in organizational communication; and the articulation of a shared vision and its realization through the lens of a specific academic community's corporate culture. The study employed the expert assessment method to identify the priority characteristics of professional self-organization, utilizing a custom-designed questionnaire, interviews, and a survey of expert respondents. Based on the analysis of empirical data, the priority characteristics of professional self-organization were identified as follows: "professional competencies," "awareness of set goals," "intrinsic motivation," "professional development," and "self-realization." The findings can be used to further develop indicators and assessment methodologies to track the dynamics of components of a higher education lecturer's professional self-organization as it develops and is actualized.

documents.abstract: The article discusses the methodological foundations of compliance with ethical standards when using artificial intelligence technologies in the educational process. The relevance of the study is due to the widespread introduction of AI into educational practice and the need to form a responsible attitude of students to its use. The paper analyzes theoretical approaches to understanding the ethical principles of using artificial intelligence, including issues of Academic Integrity, Protection of personal data and Prevention of misinformation. Particular attention is paid to the development and testing of a system of educational tasks aimed at developing students ' skills for critical analysis of content created using artificial intelligence, as well as the formation of skills for safe and ethically justified use of digital technologies. As part of the study, methods of pedagogical observation, survey, analysis of the results of educational activities and pedagogical experiment were used. The results of the study showed that the introduction of specially developed methodological approaches contributes to increasing the level of digital literacy, the development of critical thinking and the formation of sustainable skills for the ethical use of artificial intelligence tools. The obtained conclusions can be used in the development of educational programs and methodological recommendations for teachers.

The article substantiates the concept of national resilience as an emerging governance paradigm within Ukraine's state security system. Drawing on an analysis of NATO, EU, and International Organization for Standardization standards, as well as Ukrainian strategic documents, the study elucidates the distinctions between the traditional "security" paradigm and the dynamic paradigm of "resilience". The paper proposes institutional mechanisms for interagency coordination, algorithms for establishing unified situational awareness, and protocols for subsidiarity-based response and public-private partnership. It is demonstrated that resilience functions as an integrated framework for managing challenges and threats under conditions of hybrid warfare. The scientific novelty lies in the development of a matrix model for coordinating security actors that incorporates a network-centric approach into public administration. The practical significance is reflected in the applicability of the proposed mechanisms for assessing the resilience levels of public administration sectors, critical infrastructure, and cybersecurity.

documents.abstract: The article presents the results of an empirical study examining the use of large language models by first-year non-philology students during foreign language learning. The aim of the study is to investigate the frequency, patterns, purposes, and motivations behind students' use of large language models who are not majoring in a foreign language. The empirical basis of the study consists of survey results from 51 respondents in March 2026. The collected data were analyzed using both quantitative and qualitative research methods. The survey revealed that ChatGPT and Gemini are the most widely used large language models among students. The paper found that more than one-quarter of respondents use large language models daily for educational purposes. The primary motivation for using these tools is time efficiency and the desire to complete academic tasks more quickly, regardless of subject complexity. Large language models are most frequently employed for vocabulary and text translation, grammar explanation, and the completion of lexical-grammar exercises and tests. However, their potential for developing productive language skills, particularly speaking and listening, remains underutilized. The study also revealed that most students are aware that using large language models may lead to violations of academic integrity principles. At the same time, the findings suggest that students do not always have a clear understanding of the boundaries between acceptable and unacceptable uses of artificial intelligence tools in academic contexts. Based on the results obtained, methodological recommendations are proposed for integrating large language models into foreign language instruction, including the use of Text-to-Speech technologies, elements of the flipped classroom approach, and creative communicative tasks in which large language models serve as supportive learning tools.

The paper substantiates the theoretical foundations of trauma-informed education in a digital educational environment under the conditions of cognitive-information influences. The relevance stems from the fact that under conditions of prolonged military and information pressure, digital platforms that ensure the continuity of the educational process simultaneously become channels for the dissemination of emotionally charged, shocking, and traumatic content. Under such circumstances, the digital educational environment acquires the characteristics not only of a technical infrastructure for learning but also of a sociotechnical space where didactic opportunities, information threats, and psycho-emotional risks for both students and educators converge. The purpose of the paper is to substantiate the theoretical foundations of trauma-informed education in a digital educational environment during hybrid warfare by systematizing the conceptual field of the study, analysing the interconnections between war, media, and information technologies. The study is theoretical and analytical in nature, based on conceptual, comparative-analytical, systems analysis, systematization of scientific findings, and theoretical modelling. The study differentiates between war as a general reality and a source of direct traumatic experience, cognitive warfare as a targeted impact on perception, emotional responses, trust, and behaviour, and media-induced traumatization as a broader psycho-emotional phenomenon. The digital educational environment is characterized as a sociotechnical space combining didactic resources, information influences, and psycho-emotional risks. War, media, and information technologies form a shared field of influence that alters the conditions of the educational process and necessitates a trauma-informed approach. The theoretical framework of trauma-informed education is multi-component and includes trauma-sensitive, psycho-emotional safety, information-hygiene, digital-resilience, ethical-communicative, and adaptive-pedagogical components. Based on the findings, the general guidelines for adapting pedagogical practice to the conditions of intensive media influence, algorithmically reinforced content pressure, and psycho-emotional tension are outlined. Trauma-informed education in a digital educational environment serves as a promising theoretical and practical basis for reimagining pedagogical interaction under the conditions of cognitive-information influences.

Современное развитие территорий (городов) и университетов, движимое технократической логикой эффективности и инноваций, порождает риск утраты человеческого измерения. Расширяется трактовка образовательной инновации, включая в неё инфраструктуру искусственного интеллекта, что позволяет рассматривать университеты в качестве активных семиотических агентов, внедряющих эти инновации в урбанистический контекст. Цель исследования заключается в разработке и апробации методологии сравнительного семиотического анализа образовательных инноваций как инструмента трансформации городской среды в концепции «город-университет». Актуальность работы обусловлена доминированием технократической парадигмы во взаимодействии вузов и городов, что порождает риск «гуманитарного дефицита» – утраты субъектности человека и его смыслообразующей роли в образовании и урбанистическом развитии. Теоретико-методологической основой выступают: концепт «праксема» (С. С. Аванесов); подход Г. Н. Прозументовой, акцентирующий феномен «личного присутствия» и преодоление антропологического дефицита через субъективацию образования; концепция «семиотической диагностики» (И. В. Мелик-Гайказян), предлагающая паллиативное решение проблемы измерения в гуманитарных исследованиях. Исследование доказывает, что язык образовательных инноваций является критически важным фактором и индикатором гуманитарного качества трансформаций в рамках концепций «город-университет». Его анализ позволяет не только диагностировать текущие изменения, но и прогнозировать их антропологические последствия, открывая перспективы для управления развитием территорий не только как технологических, но и как подлинно человеческих, смыслонасыщенных пространств. Научная значимость исследования состоит в том, что устанавливается связь между концептом «праксема» и концепцией «семиотической диагностики» и в опоре на эту связь предлагается конкретный способ перехода от измерения количественных показателей эффективности к анализу глубинных антропологических эффектов образовательных инноваций и выявлению рисков символической дегуманизации в концепциях «город-университет». The study emphasizes that the contemporary development of territories (cities) and universities, driven by the technocratic logic of efficiency and innovation, generates the risk of losing the human dimension. The aim of the research is to develop and test a methodology of comparative semiotic analysis of educational innovations as a tool for transforming the urban environment within the “city-university” concept. The relevance of the work is determined by the dominance of the technocratic paradigm in the interaction between universities and cities, which creates the risk of a “humanitarian deficit” — the loss of human subjectivity and its meaning-forming role in education and urban development. The theoretical basis of the study is the concept of the “praxema” (S.S. Avnesov) and the approach of G.N. Prozumentova, which emphasizes the phenomenon of “personal presence” and the overcoming of the anthropological deficit through the subjectivization of education. The methodological foundation of the study is the information-synergetic approach (I.V. Melik-Gaykazyan), based on the substantiation of the following propositions: 1) the phenomenon of information is an irreversible process; 2) the information process is a mechanism of self-organization; and 3) semiotic forms are the results of stages of the information process. One of the results of this approach was the concept of “semiotic diagnostics” (I.V. Melik-Gaykazyan), the procedures of which make it possible to resolve the problem of measurement in the humanities. The method used is a humanitarian (linguosemiotic) expertise, including discourse analysis and comparative analysis of two cases: Tomsk (Russia) as a historical university center and the Lanzhou New Area (China) as a project for creating a “university-city” from scratch. The material consisted of official narratives and self-descriptions representing educational innovations in these territories. The results of the study showed that the language of educational innovations in both cases functions as a praxeme — an active tool for constructing reality. Universal traits were identified: the university is universally positioned as a “hub,” “driver,” and “bridge,” which visualizes its new active role in the city. Culturally specific differences manifested in the ways of overcoming the “humanitarian deficit.” In Tomsk, the language of innovations (narrative “guardian of traditions and the engine of the future”) is aimed at preserving the humanistic mission of the classical university and rooting innovations in the historical and cultural code. In Lanzhou, the metaphor of the “scientific-educational oasis” and the frames of integration of education and production construct a new identity for the territory and strive to overcome the alienation of the individual from education by including them in solving real development tasks. The study proves that the language of educational innovations is a critically important factor and indicator of the humanitarian quality of transformations within the frameworks of “city-university” concepts. Its analysis not only allows for diagnosing current changes but also for predicting their anthropological consequences, opening perspectives for managing the development of territories not only as technological but also as truly human, meaningful spaces. The proposed tool — humanitarian expertise — allows moving from measuring quantitative effectiveness indicators to analyzing the deep anthropological effects of educational innovations and identifying risks of symbolic dehumanization in “city-university” concepts. Expanding the interpretation of educational innovation to include artificial intelligence infrastructure makes it possible to present universities as active semiotic agents that not only introduce technology into the urban environment, but also create new anthropological meanings in it, thereby overcoming the humanitarian deficit of technocratic development.

Educational facilities have recently undergone significant, tangible technical advancements driven by the evolution of information technology. Progress in this sector manifests through the administrative development of educational institutions—a shift that inevitably impacts the student, who stands at the heart of the educational process. Students increasingly rely on electronic devices rather than traditional textbooks. This evolution is of great importance, as it paves the way for classrooms to transition from their familiar, traditional format to one that integrates artificial intelligence technologies into educational practice, This development will enable a large number of students to benefit from the advancement and grant teaching staff greater freedom in explaining curricula and conveying information using modern educational methods. documents.abstract: Background: Strained nurse-resident relations on Labor and Delivery are a widely recognized but inadequately addressed threat linked to adverse outcomes, trainee and nursing distress, hostile clinical learning environments, and patient safety issues. In our institution, a 2024 Program Evaluation Committee meeting SWOT analysis (Strength-Weakness-Opportunity-Threat) identified nurse-resident relations at a busy academic Labor and Delivery unit as an opportunity for improvement within our residency program. Issues included persistent unprofessional behaviors, inadequate and mistrusted reporting mechanisms, and a culture of silence with a fear of retaliation. Objective: To implement and evaluate a quality improvement model for improving nurse-resident relations on Labor & Delivery. Study Design: Using Kotter’s 8-Step Change Model as a framework, a multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative was launched in May 2024 as a joint effort by resident and nursing leadership. Interventions included creation of an anonymous QR code-based feedback survey, recognition of outstanding nurses and residents, monthly interdisciplinary leadership meetings to review concerns, structured social events, clarification and education regarding resident and nursing escalation pathways, and the establishment of a joint Nurse-Resident Workgroup. Results: In two years, a total of 74 nursing and resident-related incidents were submitted and addressed through the creation of an anonymous QR code-based feedback survey. In the first 7 months there were 26 submissions, in the second 7 months there were 41 submissions, and in the final 7 months there were 7 submissions. QR code submissions declined over time, which served as an indicator of culture improvement. A total of 100 kudos were submitted by both nurses and residents recognizing exemplary interprofessional behavior. Monthly nursing-initiated socials were established at the beginning of each resident rotation to intentionally strengthen camaraderie, promote teamwork, and help nurses and incoming interns build familiarity early in the rotation. As a second phase to the improvement efforts, a Nurse-Resident Workgroup was launched in November 2025, completing six structured meetings by June 2026. This workgroup consisted of a core team of 7 front-line nurses and rotating residents with a total of approximately 10 to 12 participants at each session. This in-person discussion was mediated by combined nursing and residency leadership and focused on conflict resolution and improved situational awareness between both nurses and residents without intensive investment outside of this structured time. Participants were anonymously polled at the fourth and fifth workgroup with 12/12 (100%) positive responses at the fourth workgroup and 9/10 (90%) positive responses at the fifth workgroup, with 0 negative responses in both workgroups. In addition, participants suggested 5 topics for future discussion. Conclusions: A structured and leadership-supported quality improvement initiative can meaningfully improve nurse-resident relationships on Labor and Delivery. The Nurse-Resident Workgroup is a replicable intervention that provides a structured venue for conflict resolution and improved situational awareness between nurses and residents. Discussion allows for understanding of diverse perspectives and roles, which ultimately led to system changes across nursing, residency, and faculty teams. This model provides a framework for other residency programs facing similar challenges and can be adapted to different unique Labor & Delivery environments.

CRISPR-Cas9 has entered the mainstream of genetic research and therapeutic development, offering a level of programmable and targeted gene editing that has substantially expanded the possibilities of genetic manipulation. This review focuses on the discovery to development of CRISPR-Cas9 and its recent practice in pharmacological and biotechnology field. We discuss further advancements in CRISPR technology such as high-fidelity CRISPR and new systems Cas12 and Cas13 which increases efficiency of editing and opens more opportunities. CRISPR technology has been further advanced when combined with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; guide RNA is now optimized while the off-target effects are predicted. The review also focuses on the new targets for therapy, recent trials, the legal and the social and ethical relevance of the CRISPR approach. With the development of CRISPR-Cas9 promising and revolutionary preliminary achievements in the fields of drug development and disease management and tissue engineering are anticipated. Although, in its application, there are questions that have been raised concerning side effects, carriers, and ethics, it is important to take advantage of it in the right manner. As seen in this review, CRISPR-Cas9 plays the crucial part of the development of biomedical studies and therapeutic paradigms.

Abstract The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and data science into biological research has created a growing need for computational literacy among graduate students in life science disciplines. However, many students’ entering biology-related graduate programs have limited formal training in programming, statistics, or machine learning, creating a significant barrier to engaging with modern data-driven research. The objective of this study was to evaluate baseline perceptions of AI and data science among animal science students prior to participating in a course introducing these concepts through application-based learning. A pre-course perception survey was administered to students enrolled in an introductory AI and data science course in animal science (n = 10). Survey questions used a 5-point Likert scale to assess prior programming experience, familiarity with AI concepts, attitudes toward AI applications in animal science and motivation to learn these skills. Students reported limited prior experience with programming languages (mean = 2.9 ± 1.45) and moderate use of AI tools in daily life (mean = 2.98 ± 1.32). Despite limited technical exposure, students indicated moderate understanding of basic AI and data science concepts (mean = 3.6 ± 0.70 and 3.6 ± 0.52, respectively). Participants expressed strong agreement that AI and data science can be effectively applied in animal science (mean = 3.9 ± 0.57) and that learning these skills would benefit their academic or professional development (mean = 4.0 ± 0.67). Students also expressed moderate motivation to learn AI applications in livestock systems (mean = 3.5 ± 1.08). While this project provides the current perceptions of students and their skill levels in AI and data science, a follow-up post survey to assess the effects of such a course, and combining it with a Mann-Whiteney U test will further inform the required pedagogical shifts. These preliminary findings highlight the value of interdisciplinary teaching approaches that integrate biological applications with computational methods (such as an AI in animal science course) and may inform curriculum design for graduate programs seeking to prepare life science students for increasingly data-intensive research environments.

Abstract Subclinical ketosis (SCK) is a prevalent metabolic disorder in transition dairy cows causing significant economic and welfare impacts, yet early detection remains challenging due to absent clinical signs and disease complexity. Two complementary projects developed multi-modal machine learning systems for prepartum prediction of postpartum SCK risk. The first integrated depth image-derived body shape features (extracted via CNN, anatomical keypoint sampling, and CNN-RNN), wearable sensor behavioral data, cow history, and text embeddings from farm management notes using generic and fine-tuned LLMs; Random Forest models combining image and tabular data achieved F₁ = 0.706, with fine-tuned LLM text embeddings further improving sensor-based models (F₁ 0.681 vs. 0.655). The second project added genomic data (78,964 SNPs reduced to 128 dimensions via UMAP) and introduced a cloud-based modular pipeline for automated image processing and data integration; among three fusion strategies tested, late fusion achieved the highest performance (F₁ up to 0.750) for binary SCK classification. Together, these projects show that integrating phenomic and genomic data through modern machine learning and fusion techniques substantially improves early SCK detection, supporting preventive health management in dairy farms.

documents.abstract: ABSTRACT Four-dimensional (4D) printing is an emerging additive manufacturing technology that integrates three-dimensional (3D) printing with smart materials capable of undergoing programmed changes in shape or function over time in response to specific stimuli. This technology has attracted increasing interest in pharmaceutical drug delivery because it offers the possibility of developing dynamic, programmable, and personalized drug-delivery systems. This review provides an overview of the fundamental principles of 4D printing, including stimulus-responsive mechanisms, smart materials, and major printing technologies relevant to pharmaceutical applications. Particular emphasis is placed on shape-memory polymers, hydrogels, and other responsive materials that can respond to temperature, moisture, pH, light, magnetic fields, and other environmental stimuli. Recent applications in gastroretentive, esophageal, intravesical, intestinal, transdermal, implantable, and localized drug-delivery systems are discussed, with emphasis on their potential to improve drug retention, controlled release, site-specific therapy, minimally invasive administration, and personalized treatment. The major advantages and challenges associated with pharmaceutical 4D printing are also critically evaluated, including biocompatibility, drug–material compatibility, drug stability, reproducibility, quality control, manufacturing cost, scalability, long-term material stability, regulatory requirements, and clinical translation. Finally, future perspectives involving biodegradable smart materials, multi-material printing, nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and personalized medicine are highlighted. Overall, 4D printing represents a promising approach for transforming conventional static dosage forms into dynamic and adaptive drug-delivery systems; however, comprehensive in-vitro, in-vivo, manufacturing, regulatory, and clinical studies are required to establish its safety, reproducibility, and therapeutic effectiveness. Keywords: 4D Printing, Shape Memory Polymers, Smart Drug Delivery, Stimuli-Responsive Materials, Personalized Medicine.

Abstract The enviromics approach has emerged as an efficient framework for modeling genotype-by-environment-by-management (GxExM) interactions in animal breeding. It characterizes environmental conditions (ECs) in which animals are raised using detailed environmental and management data, providing a biologically meaningful representation of environmental variability for more reliable genetic evaluation and selection of better-adapted animals. Nonetheless, the implementation of enviromics in breeding programs presents two major challenges: (i) the recurrent collection of dynamic management information from producers and (ii) the translation of multiple expected progeny differences (EPDs), estimated for each sire across ECs, into practical recommendations. To address these challenges, we developed SmartBreeder, a virtual assistant that helps Nellore producers across Brazil identify sires best suited to their local climate and soil conditions, management practices, and breeding goals. SmartBreeder was developed as a web application using TypeScript, React, and Vite for the frontend, and Supabase for backend services, with PostgreSQL for data storage and Edge Functions for server-side processing. The system follows a three-step workflow: (i) collection of environmental and management information using a structured online survey, (ii) classification of the EC based on the surveyed farm profile, and (iii) recommendation of Nellore sires with their EPDs for the predicted EC. The survey includes four sections covering general information, soil management, supplemental feeding strategies, and reproductive management. A Supabase Edge Function receives twenty-two variables from the survey and queries a large language model (Gemini 2.5) via prompt engineering with few-shot learning. The prompt incorporates a training dataset of 60 farms to assign the surveyed farm profile to one of two ECs: an intensive production system (ENV1) or an extensive production system (ENV2). The predicted EC is then used to query a PostgreSQL database containing EPDs and accuracy estimates for Nellore sires in both ECs, obtained from GxExM genetic evaluations for yearling weight, scrotal circumference, age at first calving, ribeye area, fat thickness, and marbling. The platform also highlights top-ranking sires for each trait and provides complementary information (inbreeding coefficient, pedigree, and year of birth). SmartBreeder demonstrates the potential of a virtual assistant to collect high-resolution environmental and management data directly from producers and to translate multiple EPDs from GxExM genetic evaluations into practical sire recommendations through a user-friendly interface. By integrating the enviromics approach, the platform enables ECs to be assigned independently of phenotypic records, allowing sire recommendations based on GxExM models to be extended to future years and even to farms beyond the original breeding program. This approach increases the potential impact of optimized management and precision breeding across the broader cattle population. Future deployment as Android and iOS applications will enhance accessibility and on-farm adoption. SmartBreeder, developed for Nellore cattle in Brazil, can be adapted to other breeds and regions worldwide.
topics: Genetic and phenotypic traits in livestock
Effects of Environmental Stressors on Livestock
Genetic Mapping and Diversity in Plants and Animals

documents.abstract: The Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework mitigates hallucination issues arising from questions beyond its knowledge boundaries by retrieving relevant knowledge to expand the knowledge scope of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, as the cognitive agent in the question-answering process, the RAG framework overlooks the implicit knowledge demands in complex questions, leading to a decline in the recall rate of pertinent knowledge. Furthermore, existing RAG frameworks neglect the intricate relationships among knowledge entries in the knowledge base, resulting in their reasoning processes lacking effective knowledge support. These issues indicate that the RAG framework may be misaligned with Cognitive Load Theory proposed by John Sweller during the cognitive process, thereby introducing additional cognitive load that hinder effective reasoning. To address these problems, we propose a Cognitive Hierarchy-Guided Abstract Forest Knowledge Base (CH-AFKB) based on Cognitive Load Theory. This approach conceptualizes knowledge in unstructured knowledge bases to expand the implicit knowledge within the existing knowledge base content. It also iteratively constructs an abstract forest knowledge base with ”concept-instance” characteristics from the bottom up to model relationships among knowledge entries. In experiments across three downstream tasks, the RAG framework with CH-AFKB demonstrated superior performance in most scenarios compared to strong baselines. Compared to existing RAG and LLM baselines, the CH-AFKB exhibited remarkable advantages in retrieval efficiency, knowledge integrity, and factual consistency.

Assisted reproductive technology (ART) laboratories are complex environments in which human gametes and embryos are handled through highly sensitive procedures. Because of procedural complexity, manual documentation, high workload and the need for precise identification at ev-ery step, these laboratories are inherently vulnerable to er-rors that may compromise patient safety, clinical outcomes and confidence in ART. Potential hazards may arise from equipment malfunction, human error, environmental insta-bility or deviation from validated procedures. Therefore, a comprehensive framework for risk assessment, risk man-agement and safety monitoring is essential. This review dis-cusses the main risk factors in ART laboratories and exam-ines established mitigation strategies, including witnessing systems, process mapping, key performance indicators and quality management systems. It also summarizes recom-mended procedures and case-based evidence for improving laboratory safety and performance. Current evidence indi-cates that proactive risk assessment, electronic witnessing, emerging artificial intelligence tools and strict adherence to international guidelines can reduce the likelihood of errors and support high-quality, safe patient care.
topics: Clinical Laboratory Practices and Quality Control

documents.abstract: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery combined with artificial intelligence offers unprecedented potential to improve bridge health monitoring, reducing reliance on labor-intensive and potentially hazardous manual inspections. However, the diversity of bridge types and damage categories poses significant challenges for existing convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods, which often focus on single damage types or specific bridge structures, limiting their generalization and comprehensive applicability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel dual task deep learning framework, termed bridge damage detection network (BDDNet), for simultaneous detection and segmentation of multiple surface damages across various bridge types using UAV imagery. BDDNet integrates a global attention module (GAM) within its backbone to capture long-range dependencies and enhance multiscale feature representation. Additionally, a novel APC2f module based on pinwheel convolution is incorporated into the detection branch, enlarging the receptive field and refining feature learning for small and complex damages. Extensive experiments conducted on a multitype bridge data set demonstrate that BDDNet achieves high performance, attaining approximately 85% mean average precision (mAP) in damage detection and 82% mean intersection over union (mIoU) in segmentation. Visual results further confirm the model’s ability to accurately identify and delineate diverse damages, such as rust, missing bolts, cracks, and spalling, even in complex environments with limited training data. Overall, the proposed BDDNet provides an efficient, generalizable, and practical solution for UAV-based bridge inspection, enabling comprehensive structural condition assessment and laying the foundation for future quantitative damage evaluation.

When a person approves an action while tired, the AI agent that carries it out may send a message that cannot be taken back, a refund, an alert, an account change. This note suggests a simple fix: before sending, check if the approving person showed signs of fatigue. If so, hold the message briefly for a second look before it goes out. This applies to any communication platform that sends such messages on behalf of a human or an AI agent, including Zoho CPaaS, Twilio, and Infobip.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
Personal Information Management and User Behavior
